name: Dispatcharr Stream Sort
description: Analyzes stream health, quality, and delivery performance, then scores and reorders streams already assigned to Dispatcharr channels.
author: matrix2669

fields.label: Sorting model
fields.description: Known-dead/stale streams are demoted below all usable streams before resolution is considered. Resolution remains a hard tier among streams with the same viability; bitrate, frame rate, M3U source, name rules, and delivery throughput score streams inside a tier.

fields.label: Channel scope
fields.description: Optional group/profile filters limit Analyze, Dry Run, Sort, and Analyze + Sort. Multiple values inside one filter are ORed; when both filters are set, a channel must match both.

fields.label: Channel group filter
fields.help_text: Optional exact Dispatcharr channel group names or IDs, separated by commas or new lines. Examples: Local, id:4. Empty means all groups. Uses the channel's effective group, including overrides.

fields.label: Channel profile filter
fields.help_text: Optional exact Dispatcharr channel profile names or IDs, separated by commas or new lines. Only enabled profile memberships are included. Empty means all profiles/channels.

fields.label: M3U source scores
fields.help_text: Legacy fallback. When the plugin is enabled this is replaced by one numeric score box per configured M3U account.

fields.label: Stream name scoring rules
fields.default:
# Prefix=score. Prefix rules are case-insensitive and anchored to the start of the stream name.
US=20
GO=10
TUBI=0
PRIME=-10
ROKU=-20
fields.help_text: PREFIX=score creates a case-insensitive anchored prefix rule. Advanced regex uses score::regex. All matching name rules are additive.

fields.label: Built-in incremental stream analyzer
fields.description: Analyze Streams is cache-aware. Fresh healthy streams are left alone. Dead/skipped streams are rechecked on every run; media metadata is refreshed when its TTL expires; throughput is rechecked whenever it is not healthy or its healthy TTL expires. URL changes invalidate both components.

fields.label: Stream data TTL (hours)
fields.help_text: Fresh ALIVE health/media data is reused until this TTL expires. Dead or skipped streams are rechecked every Analyze run. 0 forces media recheck on every Analyze run.

fields.label: Healthy throughput TTL (hours)
fields.help_text: HEALTHY throughput is reused until this TTL expires. Marginal, insufficient, and unknown throughput are rechecked every Analyze run. 0 forces throughput recheck on every Analyze run.

fields.label: Analysis workers
fields.help_text: Number of media checks analyzed in parallel. Keep this conservative if a provider limits simultaneous connections.

fields.label: FFprobe sample duration (seconds)
fields.help_text: Packet sample used for bitrate and metadata analysis.

fields.label: Retries for transient failures
fields.help_text: Retries timeouts, connection-refused, network-unreachable and server-error media results after the first pass.

fields.label: Per-source analysis start delay (seconds)
fields.help_text: Minimum delay between starting media checks against the same M3U account.

fields.label: Maximum streams per analysis run
fields.help_text: 0 means all unique streams attached to channels inside the selected scope. Useful for controlled dev-test runs.

fields.label: Detect fixed-duration placeholder files
fields.help_text: A continuous live stream normally has no fixed container duration. This check adds no extra provider connection.

fields.label: Detect silent audio
fields.help_text: Only applies when an audio track exists.

fields.label: Content-check sample duration (seconds)
fields.help_text: Black/frozen/silent checks share one FFmpeg decode pass.

fields.label: Integrated delivery throughput
fields.description: Throughput is now part of Analyze Streams. Healthy cached delivery results are reused; marginal, insufficient, unknown, expired, or URL-changed results are probed again. Confirmed dead media streams are not throughput-probed.

fields.label: Maximum throughput probes per minute
fields.help_text: Global start-rate cap used to limit provider load. Only streams whose throughput needs refreshing consume this allowance.

fields.label: Files
fields.description: Unified analysis/throughput cache: /data/dispatcharr_stream_sort_analysis.json | Dry-run/apply report: /data/dispatcharr_stream_sort_report.json. The old standalone throughput cache is read only as a migration fallback.

actions.label: Analyze Streams
actions.description: Incrementally refresh only stream health/media or throughput data that needs checking in the selected channel scope.

confirm.title: Analyze assigned streams?
confirm.message: Fresh healthy cached data is reused. This only opens provider connections for dead/skipped, non-healthy throughput, URL-changed, or TTL-expired data. It does not rename, move, create, or delete channels.

actions.label: Dry Run
actions.description: Calculate the proposed order for the selected channel scope without changing ChannelStream.order.

actions.label: Sort Streams
actions.description: Apply the calculated order to streams already assigned to channels inside the selected scope.

confirm.title: Apply stream ordering?
confirm.message: This changes ChannelStream.order only for the selected channel scope. It does not add or remove streams.

actions.label: Analyze + Sort
actions.description: Incrementally refresh required health/media/throughput data, then apply stream ordering.

confirm.title: Analyze and sort streams?
confirm.message: This refreshes only data that needs checking and then changes ChannelStream.order. It does not rename, move, create, or delete channels.
